cardChanges.summary: New card for the Barista Pro: dial range and start setting (manufacturer), one owner report of an upper-burr fix, a merchant listing for upper burr SP0027464 with its 2019 batch fitment cut-off, and gaps for Breville's upper-burr procedure, factory position and warranty. The Breville PDFs could not be read.

New card for the Barista Express: a merchant listing for upper burr SP0027464 with its 2019 batch fitment cut-off, a gap for Breville's upper-burr procedure (the readable retailer guide has a coarser/finer contradiction), and a dispute between two retailer pages on whether a tool is needed.

learned: Breville's US tutorial says the Barista Pro has 30 grind settings and recommends starting at 15. A reader stuck at 1 is at the far fine end of the dial range Breville describes (barista-pro/grind-settings-start-15).

One refurbished Barista Pro owner fixed gritty, fast shots by cleaning the grinder and moving the internal burr from 2 to 1. Breville offered a free replacement upper burr, but it had not arrived when the owner reported the improvement. The idea card's summary ('upper burr to 1 plus a replacement burr fixed it') overstates what the thread shows (barista-pro/owner-refurb-upper-burr-fix).

The upper burr is sold as a part (SP0027464) for both the BES870 and BES878. A seller limits it to machines with a 1926 PDC batch date or later (2019 week 26 onwards), read from the sticker underneath. Readers have to check their batch date before ordering a burr (barista-express/upper-burr-part-sp0027464, barista-pro/upper-burr-part-sp0027464).
unknowns: Breville's own upper-burr procedure, number range, factory position and warnings for the BES870 and BES878. The booklet PDFs could not be extracted in this environment, and this is the core of the troubleshooter.
Whether adjusting or replacing the upper burr affects the Breville US warranty. The answer needs a Breville support article or a direct question to support.
Whether pre-July-2019 Barista Express machines use a different upper burr (SP0001801) and a different lower burr. Search results suggest so, but the listings were rate-limited (429) and not read.
The US price and availability of a genuine upper burr from Breville. The only price seen was Australian (AUD $241.95 RRP).

Breville's documented guidance on beans, pressurised vs single-wall baskets and dose for fast shots, from the booklet Troubleshooting section, which was unreadable. The Seattle Coffee Gear guide covers some of this but is a retailer source.
How to recognise a worn upper burr, and any burr-life guidance from Breville. No source was found.
Whether the Seattle Coffee Gear product guide's mention of an included Allen key reflects an older production version. The two SCG pages disagree (barista-express/upper-burr-tool, disputed).

competitors.says: Gives clear photo-style steps for removing the burr and turning the top ring, but says to adjust the burr 'coarser' when shots are too fast at the finest setting, which is backwards. It gives no range, factory position, burr-contact warning, or check of beans, basket and dose first.

Says the factory inner-burr setting is 6 and advises moving no more than 2 steps at a time, with step-by-step removal. It does not cite Breville, name the models, or mention burr contact, warranty or worn burrs.

Owner thread where advice splits between shimming, the internal burr not being 'supposed' to be adjusted, returning the machine and buying a separate grinder. The owner's fix was cleaning plus internal burr 1, and Breville offered a free upper burr. It gives no diagnosis order.
